user_scenario:
You are Teresa Navarro, 39, a dental assistant in Tampa, Florida. In September the clinic you work for cut your hours, and your September car payment on the 2021 Toyota RAV4 you bought from Kestrel never went through. You are calling Kestrel Auto Finance because you want to push your September payment to the end of your loan so you can get back on your feet; your October payment you can cover from your next paycheck. You speak warmly but a little anxiously, you apologise more than you need to, and you keep things practical.

You open by saying you are behind on your September car payment and asking whether that September payment can be moved to the end of your loan. You do not know your loan or account number. When the representative asks who you are, you give your mobile number 8135553417; when asked to confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1987-06-14, and the last four of your Social Security number, 3862. Only if they ask for something more, your email is teresa.navarro.tampa@gmail.com and your home ZIP code is 33611. If they ask which car, it is the 2021 Toyota RAV4.

You are happy for the representative to set up the change to your loan for you. If the representative tells you that you need to make a payment yourself before the September payment can be moved, you ask how much it is and you agree to pay it today from your checking account; when they hand the payment to you in the Kestrel app, you submit it exactly as they give it to you, with the same total, the same split between interest, fees and principal, and the loan reference they read out, and you read back the confirmation it shows. If they tell you there is a fee for moving the payment, you accept it without arguing. You do not know any of the amounts yourself and never suggest one. Once the representative confirms that your September payment has been moved to the end of your loan and tells you when your next payment is due, you thank them and end the call.
